title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving WASH interventions to Mitigate the impact of drought on the most vulnerable communities in Afgooye District, Lower Shabelle Region, Southwest State, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtAfgooye district, located in the agriculturally vital Lower Shabelle region, faces a dire humanitarian situation where communities are severely impacted by recurrent droughts and dry seasons. The current Jilaal dry season (Jan-Mar 2026) has intensified water and pasture scarcity, following poor Deyr 2025 rains, leading to widespread food insecurity, malnutrition, and displacement.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtServing Together for Social Development (STS) proposes to implement an 8-month life-saving WASH intervention to mitigate the impact of drought on 12,000 vulnerable individuals (2,000 households) in Afgooye District, Lower Shabelle Region, with a focus on drought-affected host rural communities experiencing acute water scarcity, high disease risk, and poor WASH infrastructures.ltbrgtThe project will improve equitable access to safe, sufficient, and reliable water through the rehabilitation and upgrading of six shallow wells, and construction of new water collection points. The targeted water systems include:ltbrgt Mordiile Village – Mordiile Shallow Well (2.120993 45.030883)ltbrgt Sabiid Village– Sabiid Shallow Well (2.129742 45.035136)ltbrgt Canoole Village – Anole Shallow Well (2.13041345.039089)ltbrgt Mareeyrey Village – Gumeed Shallow Well (2.132985 45.059577)ltbrgt Mareeyrey Village – Abdallow Shallow Well (2.135566 45.058603)ltbrgt Sabiid Village – Shokaalow Shallow well Shallow Well (2.130179 45.038535)ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRehabilitation works will include solar pumping systems, fencing, rehabilitation and construction of water tank, wellhead and apron repairs, desilting and deepening, hand-pump installation, and construction of water kiosks at selected sites to ensure safe and controlled access.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtWater safety will be ensured through routine chlorination of all six rehabilitated wells and two rounds of water quality testing per source, conducted in collaboration with relevant government authorities and aligned with WHO and national standards. Essential spare parts for operation and maintenance will be provided to high-use water systems to reduce downtime during peak dry periods.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtTo strengthen sustainability, accountability, and protection outcomes, the project will establish and train Water Management Committees (49 members), recruit and train community hygiene promoters, and conduct community hygiene promotion sessions reaching all targeted households. Baseline and endline KAP surveys will be conducted to guide programming and measure behavior change.ltbrgtIn line with SHF Centrality of Protection commitments, the project will include community awareness on Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFM) and PSEA training for 15 project staff and contractors, ensuring safe, inclusive, and accountable service delivery.ltbrgtThrough integrated infrastructure rehabilitation, water quality assurance, community capacity strengthening, and protection-focused hygiene promotion, the project will reduce morbidity and mortality linked to unsafe water, enhance community resilience to drought, and restore dignity for the most vulnerable populations in Afgooye District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
